units.tr: Who denies that Europe once sat upon the Tyrian bull? Spanish Julia was carried off on a bull. But the one scarcely occupies a part of the star-bearing world; this one holds heaven and the gods under his sway. Why then, if the merit is equal but the fate is not, did he hold Rome more tightly in his embrace? Johannes Funccius, from Volaterranus: the cardinals who chose him were the first to feel his ingratitude. For he oppressed them all with various calamities, punishing some with exile and others with prison. He waged war against the Orsini, whom he defeated and subdued, partly through his bastard son. Thereafter he thought of nothing more than, following the example of Innocent, raising his bastards to honours, and indeed to far greater ones, since this had already begun to be a source of honour and glory among the fathers. Those most holy men were then endowed with such sanctity. From among his sons he made one, the younger, prince of Sicily; another, named Caesar Valentinus, a cardinal; and the eldest a duke in Spain. This one was soon afterwards slaughtered by night and thrown into the Tiber. Caesar the cardinal, having scorned the priesthood after his father's death, betook himself to France, carrying off a great quantity of gold. There, through the favour of King Louis, he took in marriage a kinswoman of the king of Albret, together with the town of Valence. Then, with the king's help and with lasting plunder, he acquired considerable dominion for himself in Italy, while his father Alexander was still living, who wished for nothing more than that his eldest son should become a prince. Alexander's daughter Lucretia, first known by him (a horrible crime), was given in succession to three princes. First to John Sforza, duke of Pesaro; then, when that marriage was dissolved, to Alfonso of Aragon, a bastard son of King Alfonso. When he was finally killed, she married Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara. From her epitaph, elegantly published by Giovanni Pontano, it is clear what her chastity, holiness, purity, celibacy and religion were during her father's papacy.

units.la: Hic iacet in tumulo Lucretia nomine, sed re Thais: Alexandri filia, sponsa, nurus.
units.tr: Here lies in the tomb Lucretia by name, but Thais in fact: daughter of Alexander, bride, and daughter-in-law.

units.la: In annum iubileum eiusdem Alexandri, Actius Sannazarius.
units.tr: For the jubilee year of the same Alexander, by Actius Sannazarius.

units.la: Pollicitus caelum romanus, & astra, sacerdos, Per scelera & cædes, ad Styga pandit iter.
units.tr: The Roman priest promised heaven and the stars, but through crimes and slaughter he opens the way to the Styx.
On Lucretia and Alexander, by the same:

units.la: Ergo te semper cupiet, Lucretia, Sextus? O fatum diri numinis: hic pater est?
units.tr: Will Sextus always desire you, Lucretia? O fate of a dreadful divinity: is this man your father?

units.la: Ex Eusebio captiuo Hieronymi Marij: Quid Alexandri Sexti inaudita & obscæna facta enarrem? Is cum dæmonibus fœdere inito, sese illis mo-dis omnibus addixit ac donauit, ut eorum artibus in pontificem romanum crearetur. Quod cum dæ-mones illi polliciti fuissent ac præstitissent, Alexander ita uitam suam sanctè instituere cœpit, ut nun quam aliquid facere moliretur, nisi prius dæmo-nes in consilium aduocasset. Huius pontificis haben-tur quaedam præclara, ac pontifice romano, Petri apostoli successore digna. Habentur enim illa egre-gia & notatu digna carmina, quæ huius sanctissi-mi laudes enarrant:
units.tr: From the Captive Eusebius of Girolamo Meri: Why should I recount the unheard-of and obscene deeds of Alexander VI? He entered into a covenant with demons, and bound and gave himself to them in every way, so that by their arts he might be created Roman pontiff. When those demons had promised and performed this, Alexander began to order his life so piously that he never undertook anything without first summoning the demons to counsel. There are said to be certain notable things about this Pontiff, worthy of a Roman pontiff and successor of the apostle Peter. There are indeed said to be those distinguished and memorable verses that recount the praises of this most holy man:

units.la: Vendit Alexander cruces, altaria, Christum: Emerat ille prius, uendere iure potest.
units.tr: Alexander sells crosses, altars and Christ. He had first bought them, so he has the right to sell them.

units.la: De uitio in uitium, de flamma transit in ignem, Roma sub Hispano deperit imperio.
units.tr: From vice to vice, from flame he passes into fire; Rome perishes under Spanish rule.

units.la: Sextus Tarquinus, Sextus Nero, Sextus & iste: Semper sub Sextis perdita Roma fuit.
units.tr: Sextus Tarquin, Sextus Nero, and this Sextus too: Rome was always destroyed under the Sextuses.

units.la: Hic ille Alexander est, qui Gemē Bajazetis Turcarum regis fratrem, Romae captiuum, pro ducentis aureorum millibus à Turca receptis, veneno interfecit. Hic ille inquam est, qui suam tyrannidem tueri volens, eundem Turcarum monarchā, aduersus Gallorum regem in adiutorium uocabat: & ut Neapolitanum regnum, ac Romam ipsam pro suis luxuriis, Othomannici imperij munimenta essent, effecit. Qui Antonio Mancinello, uiro doctissimo, utramque manum ac linguam abscindi iussit, quod in impios eius mores, spurcissimam uitam atque maudita sce-lera elegantem oratione scripsisset. Quis hæc sanctorum sanctissimi facta non detestetur? Sed uide qualem sit sortitus exitum. Dum parato conuiuio
units.tr: This is that Alexander who poisoned Djem, brother of Bajazet, king of the Turks, a captive at Rome, after receiving two hundred thousand gold pieces from the Turk. This, I say, is the man who, wishing to protect his tyranny, summoned that same monarch of the Turks against the king of the French as an ally; and who made the kingdom of Naples and Rome itself bulwarks of the Ottoman empire for the sake of his luxuries. He ordered both hands and the tongue of Antonio Mancinelli, a most learned man, to be cut off, because he had written, in elegant speech, against his impious morals and his most filthy life and accursed crimes. Who would not detest these deeds of the most holy of the holy? But see what end he met. While he was preparing a banquet, having ordered several wealthy senators and cardinals to be killed with the same kind of poison by which he had killed Djem, it happened that, through the carelessness of those who were handing round the cups, the flask was swapped, and Alexander himself drank the poison, and so perished together with those senators and cardinals.

units.la: opulentos aliquot senatores ac Cardinales eodem veneni genere, quo Gemen occiderat, interfici mandasset, contigit ut incaute ab his qui pocula porrigebant, mutata lagena, Alexander & ipse venenum hauserit: sicq; una cum senatoribus illis ac Cardinalibus perierit.
units.tr: having ordered several wealthy senators and cardinals to be killed with the same kind of poison by which Gem had died, it happened that, through the carelessness of those who were handing round the cups, the flagon was switched, and Alexander himself drank the poison; and so he perished together with those senators and cardinals.

units.la: Huius sequitur epitaphium, authore Actio Sannazario:
units.tr: Here follows an epitaph, by the author Actius Sannazarius:

units.la: Seuitiæ, insidiæ, rabies, furor, ira, libido, Sanguinis & diri spongia, dira sitis, Sextus Alexander iaceo hic, jam libera gaude Romæ: tibi quoniam mors mea, vita fuit.
units.tr: Cruelty, treachery, rage, fury, anger, lust, the sponge of blood and dire thirst: I, Sextus Alexander, lie here. Rejoice now, free Rome, for my death was your life.

units.la: Sub hoc pontifice Hispano vix esse fertur Petrus Mendez, etiam Hispanus, Cardinalis Valentinensis, qui non meretricum agmine, ac sub rege Ferdinando, regina ipsa satiatus, petijt atq; obtinuit ab eodem sanctissimo diaboli vicario, ut & suo filio notho Zanetensi Marchione, in sacro cœlibatu, tanquam amata sponsa uteretur. Talis est horum diabolorum cœlibatus, per totum orbe jactatus.
units.tr: Under this Spanish pontiff, it is said that Pedro Mendez, also a Spaniard and Cardinal of Valencia, was hardly satisfied by a crowd of prostitutes. Under King Ferdinand, having been sated by the queen herself, he sought and obtained from the same most holy vicar of the devil that he might have the use of his natural son, the Marquis of Zanete, in holy celibacy, as if he were a beloved bride. Such is the celibacy of these devils, which is bandied about through the whole world.

units.la: Anno Domini 1499. exustus est Florentia celeberrimus concionator, Hieronymus Savonarola, monachus Dominicanus, vir eruditione ac pietate insignis, cum aliquot sociis. Communionem sub utraque specie ipse defendit. Indul-gentias damnavit. Papae, Cardinalium, omniumq; spiritualium turpem, sceleratamq; vitam, & officii neglectionem, grauissimè est accusare solitus. Negauit etiam primum Papæ Clauis docuit, ecclesiæ toti, non uni Petro traditas ad hæc, Papam nec uitam, nec doctrinam Christi retinere dicebat: quia plus suis indulgentijs & traditiunculis, quàm Christi merito tribueret, ideoq; eum esse Antichristum. Asseruit quoq;, Papæ excommunicationes timendas non esse. Prædixit item futura quaedam: nempe uastitatem Florentiæ & Romæ, atq; tandem instaurationem ecclesiæ: quæ omnia hac nostra memoria acciderunt. Quare etiam à Ioanne Francisco Pico, Mirandulano comite, sanctus propheta appellatur, & proprio scripto contra Papam defenditur. Defendunt & alij quidam docti uiri eiusdem Sauonarolæ innocentiam. Tribuunt ei quoq; Marsilius Ficinus in quadam epistola, & Philippus Cominæus in historia Gallica, prophéticum spiritum.
units.tr: In the year of the Lord 1499, the most celebrated preacher Girolamo Savonarola, a Dominican friar, a man distinguished for learning and piety, was burnt at Florence together with several companions. He himself defended communion under both kinds. He condemned indulgences. He was accustomed to denounce most severely the shameful and wicked lives and the neglect of duty of the Pope, the cardinals and all the spiritual men. He also denied that the keys were first given to the Pope, and taught that they were given to the whole Church, not to Peter alone. He said that the Pope retained neither the life nor the teaching of Christ, because he attributed more to his indulgences and little traditions than to Christ's merit, and therefore that he was Antichrist. He also asserted that papal excommunications were not to be feared. He likewise foretold certain future events: namely the devastation of Florence and Rome, and at last the restoration of the Church, all of which came to pass in our own memory. For this reason also Giovanni Francesco Pico, count of Mirandola, calls him a holy prophet, and defends him against the Pope in a writing of his own. Certain other learned men also defend the innocence of this Savonarola. Marsilio Ficino, in a certain letter, and Philippe de Commynes, in his history of Gaul, also ascribe to him a prophetic spirit.
161. Pius the Third.

units.la: Pius tertius, natione Hetrusca, patria Senensis, Pij secundi ex Laodamia sorore nepos, & Franciscus Picolhomineus antea uocatus: prædicto Alexandro post cotentiones, Cardinalium suffragijs in eadem sede successit. Post patris mortem, Va-lentinus lentinus Borgia eius thesaurum omnem corripiēs, Vaticanum Papalis electionis locum, duodecim armatorum millibus muniuit, ea intentione, ut Cardinales in sua uota compelleret. Ipsi uero Cardinales, ad periculum illud euitandum, in ædem Minervæ se statim congregabant: & ab eo mox circundati erant. Fama autem inde peruagante, captos esse patres, & direptiones ac cædes tota urbe fieri, omnes illico pauor invasit. Tabernæ postea claudebantur, arma corripiebantur, transtris, trabibus, catenisq; ferreis uiarum exitus obstruebatur, haud aliter quàm si rursus Hannibal mœnia tenuisset. Ille autem, quòd duram forte provinciam assumpsisse uideretur, rogatusq; à patribus, ut à talipertinacia desisteret, paulo mox se obtemperaturum polliceabatur. Cum ergo electus esset hic Pius, depositæ feritate Valetinus gratias egit Cardinalibus, quòd quem maximè cupiebat, ordinassent Papam. Ille pontifex statim, contra Gallos Italiam occupātes, conspirationem fecit: indignè ferens, Apuliam & magnam Italiæ partem eorum regem sibi subegisse. Sperabat affuturum diem, quo insidiarum tendiculis circunduttum Gallum (bonus Papa) damnis afflegeret: ac tandem coniuratorum ope, terris illis exploderet. Sed interim, dum hæc studeret, ex ulcere cruris, quo diu laborauerat, 27. post suam creationem[?] die decessit, eodem anno Domini 1503, quo prædictus Alexander, quintodecimo Calendas novembris: nihilo rerum ab se gesto, quas maximas animo conceperat. Nam præter bellum Gallicum, & Ecclesiam reformare, concilium celebrare, ac in Turcas profecisci avunculi sui imitatione statuerat.
units.tr: Pius the Third, a Tuscan by nation, from Siena, grandson of Pius the Second through his sister Laodamia, and formerly called Francesco Piccolomini, succeeded the aforesaid Alexander in the same see after contentions, by the votes of the cardinals. After his father's death, Valentinus Borgia seized all his treasure and fortified the Vatican, the place of the papal election, with twelve thousand armed men, with the intention of forcing the cardinals to his wishes. The cardinals themselves, to avoid that danger, at once gathered in the church of Minerva, and were soon surrounded by him. Then, when the report spread that the fathers had been seized and that plunder and slaughter were taking place throughout the city, panic seized everyone at once. Shops were then closed, arms were seized, and the exits of the streets were blocked with beams, timbers and iron chains, just as if Hannibal had again taken the walls. He, however, because he seemed to have undertaken a hard task, and was asked by the fathers to give up such obstinacy, promised that he would soon comply. When this Pius was therefore elected, Valentinus, laying aside his fierceness, thanked the cardinals because they had made Pope the man he most desired. That pontiff at once made a conspiracy against the French who were occupying Italy, taking it ill that their king had subdued Apulia and a large part of Italy to himself. He hoped that a day would come when he would entangle the Frenchman in the snares of plots (good Pope) and crush him with losses, and at last, with the help of the conspirators, drive him out of those lands. But meanwhile, while he was busy with these things, he died of an ulcer on his leg, from which he had long suffered, on the 27th day after his creation[?], in the same year of the Lord 1503 in which the aforesaid Alexander died, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of November: having accomplished nothing of the great things he had conceived in his mind. For besides the war against the French, he had resolved to reform the Church, to hold a council, and to set out against the Turks in imitation of his uncle.

units.la: In huius quartæ sectionis fine, ex præteritis claret, quod adhuc sidera in terram collapsa, Apoc. 9. etiam sint hi pontifices quadraginta & unus, quos ab Innocentio quarto recitavimus, propter absolutam, plenam & perfectam eorum à Christo defectionem, per execrabilissimas idololatrias, tyrannides & luxurias. Et eius generis erant sub Dracone magno quadraginta pontifices, ac nunc sub Abadone peremptore quadraginta & unus, qui simul faciunt octoginta & unum numero. Horum primus à Syl-vestro secundo ad Innocentium quartum, data est clavis abyssi Tartarea, ut ex eius horribili fumo locustas voratrices in Christianas regiones emit-terent, ut suæ iniquitatis illic operentur mysteria. Posterioribus autem ab eodem Innocentio ad Ju-lium secundum, concessum est, ut eas nutrirent ad omnis veritatis obscurationem: ut impostricib. do-ctrinis[?] ac mendacibus signis deciperent, si possibile fit, etiam ipsos Dei electos, Matth. 24. Nam Draco ille magnus, qui & Satan ipse, Angelus est Abyssi, idem[?] Abadon, Locustarum formidabilium, fra-terculorum scilicet Mendicantium, ac Missantium sacrificulorum rex, Latine vastator, exterminator, perditor, peremptor. Hi enim perfida ac pestilenti doctrina decretorum Papalium, sententiarum Lombardicarum, ordinariarum quaestionum, determinationum, quodlibetorum, summarum, fratriumq; sermonum & consimilium nugarum, in numeros ad gehennam, à praedicto Innocentio per 260 annos trahebant. Ita ut sint huius generis pontifices & doctores per pallidum equum significati, cuius sessor est mors tum corporis tum animae, quam sequitur infernus, Apoc.6. Per ignes hi etiam, insatiabili tyrannide, per aquas, laqueos, gladios, atq; omnium mortium genera, perditissimi nebulones, sanctissimorum veritatis Dei testium corpora indies perdunt, quod Abadoni eorum regi obedire relicto Christo contemnant. Exemplo hi diebus in Anglia nobis sunt, Polus Cardinalis, Spurius Bonerus, Vuhitus perfidus, & alij adhuc multi, Antichristi ac diaboli laniones. Ab his lupis rapacibus suam sponsam Ecclesiam misericorditer liberet Deus noster optimus maximus. Amen.
units.tr: At the end of this fourth section, it is clear from what has gone before that the stars fallen to earth, Rev. 9, are also these forty-one popes whom we listed from Innocent IV, on account of their complete, full and perfect defection from Christ, through most execrable idolatries, tyrannies and lusts. Of this kind were the forty popes under the great Dragon, and now the forty-one under the destroyer Abaddon, which together make eighty-one in number. Of these, the first, from Sylvester II to Innocent IV, was given the key of the Tartarean abyss, so that from its horrible smoke they might send out devouring locusts into Christian regions, to work there the mysteries of their iniquity. But to the later ones, from the same Innocent to Julius II, it was granted that they should nourish them for the obscuring of all truth: so that they might deceive, with false doctrines and lying signs, if it were possible, even God's elect, Matt. 24. For that great Dragon, who is also Satan himself, is the angel of the abyss, the same Abaddon, king of the formidable locusts, that is, of the Mendicant friars and the Mass-saying little priests; in Latin, the devastator, exterminator, destroyer, slayer. For these men, by the perfidious and pestilent doctrine of papal decretals, Lombard's sentences, ordinary questions, determinations, quodlibets, summas, friars' sermons and similar trifles, for 260 years from the aforesaid Innocent were drawing people in numbers to Gehenna. So the popes and teachers of this kind are signified by the pale horse, whose rider is death of body and soul, followed by hell, Rev. 6. By fires too, with insatiable tyranny, by waters, snares, swords and every kind of death, these most abandoned scoundrels daily destroy the bodies of the most holy witnesses of God's truth, because, having forsaken Christ, they scorn to obey Abaddon their king. Examples of these are with us in England: Cardinal Pole, the bastard Bonner, the treacherous Vuhitus, and many others still, butchers of Antichrist and of the devil. May our most good and most great God mercifully free his bride, the Church, from these ravening wolves. Amen.

units.la: TERTIAE classis sectio quinta, de Papis, uel Romanis Antichristis, sub casu regni papistici, per Dei uerbum, 2. Thes. 2. & Dan. 8. usque ad mundi finem.
units.tr: Section Five of the Third Class, concerning the Popes, or Roman Antichrists, under the collapse of the papal kingdom, by the Word of God, 2 Thess. 2 and Dan. 8, until the end of the world.

units.la: AB Innocentio quarto, qui sectarum Mendicantium insignis proue&or extitit, ac nobilitator, per 260 annos hucusque, hoc est, ad annum à nato Seruatore 1503. Antichristum Abadonem in omnibus fi-ctis expressit. Angelus abyssi Abadon ille primum erat, à daemoniorum principe in terra ad hoc missus, ut in suo vicario, Papa Romano, potenter per illam aetatem regnaret. In hunc finem quoque, non solum ut fidem ex audito Christi verbo coeptam, per illum corrumperet, sed & electam Dei sponsam ecclesiam ab eius copula separaret ac perderet. Habebat ille ad id pertinaciter operandum, ipsius Abyssi clauem, hoc est, tenebrarum ac caeci-tatum infernalium potestatem: ut quae lucidae veri-tatis sunt, per somnia sophistica confunderet. Ex eo Tartareo fonte turmatim locustae volitabant: qui sunt Mendicantium ordinum fraterculi, cum rasis missatoribus ac loquacibus sophistis. Hi Abadonem assumpserant in suum regem: pro patre sanctissimo illum
units.tr: From Innocent IV, who was the notable patron and ennobler of the Mendicant orders, for 260 years down to the year 1503 from the birth of our Saviour, he expressed Antichrist Abaddon in all his fictions. That angel of the bottomless pit, Abaddon, was first sent into the earth by the prince of demons, so that he might reign powerfully in that age through his vicar, the Roman Pope. To this end also he worked, not only to corrupt the faith begun from the hearing of Christ's Word, but also to separate and destroy the chosen Church, God's bride, from her union with Christ. He had for this stubborn work the key of the abyss itself, that is, the power of darkness and infernal blindness, so that he might confound with sophistical dreams what belongs to the light of truth. From that Tartarean well the locusts flew out in swarms, that is, the little friars of the Mendicant orders, with their shaven missionaries and garrulous sophists. These had taken Abaddon as their king, and always acknowledged him as the holy father, and as the supreme head of the universal Church.

units.la: Ioan. illum semper agnoscebant, & pro universalis Ecclesiae capite supremo. Alios praepositos aut magistratus minime curabant, dum essent per eius bullas ab omni potentissimorum principum iurisdictione exempti: & reges Caesarem ipsum, illius dominio subiici debere, ex cathedris ac pulpitis docerent. Hoc luce clarius sub Innocentio quarto patebat: qui eorum suffurris[?] Fridericum tertium excommunicavit, imperioque tyrannice privavit. Thomas Aquinas & alii sophistae, subtilissimis elenchis Papam Dei vicarium faciebant: & ille vicissim eos in sanctos Ecclesiae doctores admisit. Quid autem magnus eorum in Anglia nostra numerus, cum suis sententiis, summulis, decretis, determinationibus, quaestionibus, quodlibetis aut aliis diabolorum factis egerit, in praecedentibus centuriis satis indicatum est. A factis cognoscuntur locustae, & a friuola doctrina[?] fraterculi. Deinceps enim, ab anno Domini 1503. sub Iulio secundo, qui tyrannicus bellator erat, & suis successoribus, usque ad ultimi iudicis aduentum, Papatus ruinam patietur. Diminuta est Diaboli in Antichristo potestas decipiendi, & indies magis ac magis diminuetur: at saeuiendi in electos Dei, non item. Signa futuri lapsus aut ruinae papistici regni plura Iulium praecesserunt. Ioannes 24. a bubone quodam mirabiliter, ut dictum est. est, molestatus fuit: & in itinere uersus Constanti-am ex rheda sua cecidit. Ignominiose depositus ili-[?]lic erat: declaratumq; fuit generale concilium habere potestatem in Papam. Vnde eius atq; Pauli secundi tempore res Pontificia ad magnam inclinationem uenit: semperq; in peius ruit. Sub Alexā drisexti regimine, Angelus supremus ex Hadriani mole in Tiberim cecidit, terrifico deiectus[?] fulmine. Quæ à Julio secundo, qui D. Petri clauem in Tibe-rim proiecit, infortunia hucusq; succreuerint, vix ulli sunt qui ignorant. Juxta D. Pauli prophetiam, impium illum Antichristum Christus conficiet spi-ritu oris sui, aduentusq; sui claritate delebit. Vi-vus mittetur (inquit Angelus ad Joannem) in stag-num ardentis ignis ac sulphuris, Apoc. 19. ubi cru-cietur in sempiternum. Fiat, fiat: Amen.
units.tr: Ioan. They cared little for other prelates or magistrates, since by his bulls they were exempt from the jurisdiction of all the most powerful princes. And from their chairs and pulpits they taught that kings, and Caesar himself, ought to be subject to his dominion. This was plainer than daylight under Innocent IV, who excommunicated Frederick III through their plots and tyrannically deprived him of the empire. Thomas Aquinas and other sophists, with the subtlest arguments, made the Pope the vicar of God, and he in turn admitted them among the holy teachers of the Church. What a great number of them there were in our England, with their opinions, summaries, decrees, determinations, questions, quodlibets and other devilish deeds, has been sufficiently shown in the preceding centuries. The locusts are known by their deeds, and the little friars by their frivolous teaching. From the year of the Lord 1503, under Julius II, who was a tyrannical warrior, and his successors, the papacy will suffer its ruin until the coming of the final judge. The power of the Devil to deceive in Antichrist has been diminished, and day by day it will be diminished more and more; but his power to rage against the elect of God has not been diminished. Several signs of the coming fall or ruin of the papal kingdom went before Julius. John XXIII, as has been said, was wonderfully troubled by a certain bubo, and on the journey toward Constance he fell from his carriage. He was deposed in disgrace, and it was declared that a general council has power over the Pope. Hence under Eugenius and Paul II the Pontifical affair came to a great decline, and it has always gone from bad to worse. Under the government of Alexander VI the chief angel fell from the mass of Hadrian into the Tiber, cast down by a terrifying thunderbolt. Hardly anyone is ignorant of the misfortunes that have grown up since Julius II, who threw the keys of St Peter into the Tiber. According to the prophecy of St Paul, Christ will destroy that impious Antichrist with the Spirit of his mouth, and will blot him out by the brightness of his coming. "He will be cast alive," says the angel to John, "into the lake of burning fire and brimstone," Rev. 19, "where he will be tormented for ever." So be it, so be it: Amen.
162, Julius II.

units.la: Julius secundus, patria Genuensis, Sixti quarti Ro-mani olim pontificis, nepos (si non filius) & Julia-nus Ruerius antea nuncupatus, ex presbytero Cardinale, titulo S. Petri ad vincula, in magnum Dei adversarium, Papam, assumebatur. Virum bonum, Stella Venetus, hunc perditionis filium in Pontifi-cum catalogo vocat: & tanto (quod facile credo) taliqz principatu dignissimum. Ita de illis sunt gloriati adulatores Papicolæ, quibus propheta Dei sanctus maledixit, dicens: Væ qui dicitis malum bonum, & bonum malum, ponentes tenebras lucem, &c. Esa.5. Ea enim quæ ad Christianæ religionis dignitatem pertinere Stella in hoc Iulio arbitrabatur, ad Satanæ monarchiam & æternæ perditionis regnum horribiliter spectare dignoscuntur. Et revera curiosò illa circumspexit animo Iulius, imuerecundus Antichristus, ac bellator iniquissimus, ut Stellæ verba prosequar. Miram quoque pietatem, eius immanem tyrannidem assentator & hypocrita nominat: prudentiam astum, sapientiam dolum, consilium fraudem. Taliq; pontifice ac nauclero Ecclesiam indigere pronunciat, qui Petri naviculam ad salutis portum redigere posset: ac si horribilium uitiorum omnium sentina, mana synagoga & Babylonica meretrix, ea ipsa esset in mysterio cymba, ac sordidissimus Iulius Christus ipse. Multo rectius de hoc incarnato diabolo Vuicelius, æstimator alioqui iniquus, sentit: Martiquam Christo deditiorem illum fuisse contestans. Eius impudentissima facta in Appendicibus maioris nostri operis lectori uidenda se offerunt. De eius insania dum iret ad bellum, proiectus in Tiberim D. Petri clauibus, sic scribit inter alios Philippus Melanchthon:
units.tr: Julius II, a native of Genoa, formerly nephew (if not son) of the Roman pontiff Sixtus IV, and previously called Giuliano della Rovere, was raised from a presbyter cardinal with the title of St Peter in Chains to be the great adversary of God, the Pope. The Venetian Stella calls this son of perdition a good man, in the catalogue of Popes, and (as I easily believe) most worthy of such a principate. So did the flatterers of the Papists boast of these men, whom God's holy prophet cursed, saying: "Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil, who put darkness for light," etc., Isa. 5. For those things which Stella thought in this Julius pertained to the dignity of the Christian religion, are known to point horribly toward the monarchy of Satan and the kingdom of eternal perdition. And indeed Julius, the shameless Antichrist and most unjust warrior, looked about in that way with his mind, to follow Stella's words. This flatterer and hypocrite calls his monstrous tyranny a wonderful piety; his prudence he calls cunning, his wisdom deceit, his counsel fraud. He declares that the Church needed such a pontiff and pilot as could steer Peter's little boat into the harbour of salvation, as if this very man were the cesspool of all horrible vices, the Jewish synagogue and the Babylonian harlot, and the most filthy Julius were Christ himself, in the mystery of the boat. Vuicelius, otherwise an unfair judge, judges far more rightly of this incarnate devil, testifying that he was more devoted to Mars than to Christ. His most shameless deeds present themselves to the reader to be seen in the Appendices of our larger work. About his madness when he went to war, and was cast into the Tiber with St Peter's keys, Philip Melanchthon writes among others in this way:

units.la: Cum contra Gallos bellum Papa Iulius effet / Gesturus, sicut fama uetusta docet: / Ingentes Martis turmas contraxit & urbem / Egressus, saeuas edidit ore minas. / Iratusque sacras clauis in flumina iecit / Tibridis, hic urbi pons ubi iungit aquas. / Inde manu strictum uagina deripit ensem, / Exclamansque truci talia uoce refert: / Hic gladius Pauli nos nunc defendet ab hoste, / Quandoquidem clauis nil iuuat ista Petri,
units.tr: When Pope Julius was about to wage war against the Gauls, as ancient report teaches, he gathered huge troops of Mars and, going out from the city, uttered savage threats with his mouth. And angry, he threw the sacred keys into the waters of the Tiber, where the bridge joins the waters to the city. Then he snatched a sword drawn from its sheath with his hand, and crying out with a fierce voice he said these things: "This sword of Paul will now defend us from the enemy, since the keys of Peter are of no help at all."

units.la: Gaspari Bruschii locus de eodem Iulio.
units.tr: Gaspar Bruschius's passage about the same Julius.

units.la: Iulius aduersum Romae egressurus in hostem, / Magne sub imperio Maximiliane tuo: / Clauibus in Tiberim proiectis, ocyus ensem / Fulmineum arripiens, talia laetus ait: / Quandoquidem Petri nil nos iuuat aurea clauis, / Arma, arma & gladios experiamur eos, / Quos Paulus nostra Tarsensis in urbe reliquit: / Forsitan hi melius limina nostra tegent.
units.tr: Julius, marching out of Rome against the enemy, under your rule, great Maximilian: after throwing the keys into the Tiber, he snatched up the thunderbolt-like sword and joyfully said: "Since the golden key of Peter does us no good, let us take up arms, arms and swords, and try those which Paul of Tarsus left in our city. Perhaps these will guard our threshold better."

units.la: Sic nunc pontifices etiam magis arma requirunt, / Quàm clauis doceant ut Galilaee tuas. / At quanto melius facerent, & rectius ipsis / Consulerent sibi, consulerentq; suis: / Si veram fidei pietatem, & tam manifestam, / Haec spargi sinerent dogmata vera Dei,
units.tr: So now the pontiffs seek arms even more than they teach your Galilean doctrines. But how much better would they do, and how much more wisely would they consult for themselves and their people, if they allowed the true doctrines of God to spread, the true piety of faith, so plain and clear,

units.la: Quæ Paulus quondam & Petrus docuere, docetq; Germani hoc nostro tempore mille uiri?
units.tr: which Paul and Peter once taught, and which a thousand Germans in our own time teach?
Huldrych Hutten on the sword of Julius.

units.la: Ille sui[?] longo successor in ordine Petri, More nouo tantas res agit, & studio, Nam neq; pro populis orat, pacíq; relictus, Quod faceret Petrus, sacra fidemq; docet: Verum bella mouet, gerit arma, & sanguine gaudet[?]. Nimirum Paulu prætulit ille Petro. Paulus habet gladium, sed non ferit: occidit illo. At malus hic multis intulit exitium.
units.tr: That man, the successor of Peter in a long line, pursues such great affairs in a new fashion and with zeal. For he does not pray for the peoples, nor does he teach what Peter did, the sacred faith and peace he left behind. Rather he stirs up wars, wages arms, and rejoices in blood. Surely he has preferred Paul to Peter. Paul had a sword, but did not strike; by it he killed. But this wicked man has brought destruction on many.
Description of Julius, by the same Hutten.

units.la: Qui chalybe & duris amicitur Iulius armis, Terribilis barba, terribilisq; coma: Cui torvos horrore oculos frons occulit atrox, Tartareæ ignescunt cuius in ore minæ: Ille inquam gladijs, atq; occidente sagitta Et terra populis, & metuendus aquis: Qui trucibus reges terrarum innexuit armis, Qui tetrum excito fuit in orbe malum: Ille tot exitiorum & tanti criminis author, Quo se cum populis imminuere duces, Quiq; manu, quiq; ingenio dira omnia patrat, Natus in humanum pestis acerba genus.
units.tr: Julius, clothed in steel and hard arms, terrible in beard and terrible in hair, whose savage eyes are hidden beneath a fierce and horrid brow, whose threats blaze forth from a Tartarean mouth: he, I say, feared by peoples on land and by waters, with sword and with arrow that flies by night; who has bound kings of the earth with fierce arms, who has stirred up a foul evil in the world; he, the author of so many ruins and of so great a crime, by whom the leaders have diminished themselves along with their peoples; who with hand and with wit performs all dreadful deeds, a bitter pestilence born to the human race.

units.la: Cuius opus mors est, turpissimus ocia luxus, Qui pacem cunctis abstulit, arma dedit: Ille inquam talis cum uita & moribus extet, Dissimilis Christo, dissimilisq; Petro: Quid facit, aut quid habet, quod tandem dicere Dignum Romani nomine pontificis?
units.tr: His work is death, his leisure the most shameful luxury; he has taken peace from all and given arms. He, I say, who has such a life and such morals, unlike Christ and unlike Peter: what does he do, or what does he have, that can at last be called worthy of the name of Roman pontiff?
On the indulgences of Julius, by the same author.

units.la: Fraude capit totum mercator Iulius orbem: Vendit enim coelos, non habet ipse tamen. Vende mihi quod habes. nam qui pudor, ut mihi uè Ipsum te Iuli cuius egere uides? Quin fera Centimanos emittas terra Gigantes, Iulius expulso uendat ut astra loue. Donec enim coelos alius regit, & tonat inde, Non ego tam magni muneris emptor ero.
units.tr: Julius the merchant captures the whole world by fraud: for he sells heaven, though he does not himself possess it. Sell me what you have. For what shame is it, Julius, that you see yourself in need of what you sell? Rather let the savage earth send forth her hundred-handed giants, so that Julius might sell the stars once Jupiter is cast out. For as long as another rules heaven and thunders from there, I will not be the buyer of so great a gift.

units.la: Plura Iulius ille à Christianis principibus diris & armis crudeliter extorsit, occisis intra septen- nium eius immani tyrannide plusquam ducentis Chri- stianorum hominum absq; ulla tantæ iacturæ com- miseratione, millibus. Pro uictoriis autem quibus post tantum sanguinem effusum tyrannus gaude- bat, Helvetios perpetuo ecclesiasticæ libertatis de- sensorum titulo donavit, cum publicis bellorum si- gnis, uexillis, bullatis priuilegijs, aureo gladio ac pileo. A Gallo tamen postea ad Rauennā ingenti praeprælio superabatur. Obijtq; demum post cædes innumeras atq; inaudita scelera horrendum hoc modo strum, anno Christi 1513 vicesimoprimo die Februa-rij, durante adhuc concilio, quod Romæ fallaciter celebrandum indixerat.
units.tr: That Julius extorted many things from Christian princes cruelly, with dreadful arms, and within seven years of his monstrous tyranny more than two hundred thousand Christian men were slain, without any pity for so great a loss. For the victories, however, over which the tyrant rejoiced after so much blood had been shed, he bestowed on the Swiss the title of perpetual defenders of ecclesiastical liberty, together with public battle standards, banners, sealed privileges, a golden sword and a cap. Yet he was afterwards defeated by the French in a great battle at Ravenna. At last, after countless slaughters and unheard-of crimes, he died in this horrible manner, on the twenty-first day of February in the year of Christ 1513, while the council, which he had deceitfully appointed to be held at Rome, was still going on.

units.la: Ex commentarijs Ioannis Funccij: Is Iulius quum parentibus natus effet obscuris, fortunæ beneficio, suaq; industria (ambitione ac nummis) per gradus ascendens, ad summum peruenit, vir acri & ver-suto ingenio, atque ad bella præcipuè natus, Petri patrimonium armis Nimrodico more auxit. Rauen-nam à Venetis occupatam grauissima cinxit obsi-dione: quam tandem expugnatam, suo adiunxit im-perio. Simili ferocitate Seruiam, Imolam, Fauen-tiam, Foroliuium, Bononiam, & alias urbes, è prin-cipum manibus rapuit, non sine effuso multorum san-guine. Ex Ioannis Sleidani chronico: Cum effet creatus pontifex Iulius, iureiurando promisit concilium se habiturum esse intra biennium. Cum autem bellis Italiam turbaret, nunc Venetorum, nunc Galliæ regis, nunc Ferrariæ Ducis, nunc Bentiuolo-rum Bononiensium hostis: Cardinales numero novem, secessione facta, cum Mediolanum venissent, concilium indicunt ad urbem Pisanam. Inter hos erant præcipui: Bernardinus Cruceius, Guilhelmus Prænestinus, Franciscus Coffentinus: ijsq; sese con-iuniunxerant Maximiliani Caesaris & Ludouici duodecimi Galliarum regis procuratores, qui idem agebant. Indictum uero fuit concilium anno salutis 1511. Maij die 19. ut calendis deinde Septembris in choaretur. Indicendi causam adferunt, quod ille iniurandum violarit, quod tot annorum pontifex concilij spem nullam praebeat: & quoniam grauissima sint crimina, de quibus ipsum accusare uelint. Erat ipsorum consilij, remouere illum magistratu, quem per largitionem & ambitum acquisisset. Iulius uero, grauissima denunciata poena, mandat, ne quis omnium illius pareat: & concilium aliud indi-cit in proximum annum, ad 19. Aprilis inchoandū Romae, in aede Lateranensi, cui subscripserunt 21. Cardinales, hoc enim artis esse pontificiae dicunt, quando concilium declinant, ut alterum alicubi loco ipsis opportuno denuncient.
units.tr: From the commentaries of John Funccius: Julius, though he was born of obscure parents, rose step by step by the favour of fortune and by his own industry (ambition and money), and reached the summit, a man of keen and crafty wit, born especially for wars, who by Nimrod's manner increased the patrimony of Peter by arms. He laid a very severe siege to Ravenna, which had been seized by the Venetians; when at last he had stormed it, he added it to his empire. With like ferocity he snatched Siena, Imola, Faenza, Forlì, Bologna and other cities from the hands of princes, not without the blood of many poured out. From the chronicle of John Sleidan: When Julius had been created pontiff, he promised under oath that he would hold a council within two years. But since he kept troubling Italy with wars, now as the enemy of the Venetians, now of the king of France, now of the duke of Ferrara, now of the Bentivogli of Bologna, nine cardinals, having withdrawn, came to Milan and appointed a council to be held at the city of Pisa. Among these the most prominent were Bernardino Carvajal, William of Palestrina and Francis of Cosenza; and joined with them were the agents of the emperor Maximilian and of Louis XII, king of France, who were pursuing the same aim. The council was indeed announced for the year of salvation 1511, on the nineteenth day of May, to begin at the calends of September. They gave as the reasons for convening it that he had violated his oath, that the pontiff over so many years offered no hope of a council, and that the charges they wished to bring against him were very grave. It was their purpose to remove him from the office which he had acquired by bribery and ambition. But Julius, having denounced the gravest penalty, ordered that no one of all should obey him; and he appointed another council for the following year, to begin on the nineteenth of April at Rome, in the Lateran basilica, which was signed by twenty-one cardinals, for they say it is a mark of papal skill that, when they avoid a council, they proclaim another somewhere at a place convenient for themselves.

units.la: Erat tum papiae iurisconsultus magni nominis, Philippus Decius: hic edito scripto, Cardinalium causam aduersus pontificem defendebat. Ex Maf-sei 20 Chronicorum libro: Francorum rex, intelligens papam Iulium, iunctis Venetis moliri quiddā contra suos, in praesidijs constitutos, coegit concilium apud Turonos mense Septembri, ubi propositae sunt has quaestiones: An licitum sit papae, mouere bellum in aliquem principem sine causa? An talis princeps defendendo sua, possit invadere impetito-rem, & ab eius obedientia se subtrahere? Responsum est: Non licere Pontifici. Licere autem principi, facere quod quaerebatur. Observandam etiam pragmaticam sanctionem per regnum Fracie[?]. Nec curandum esse de censuris iniustis, si fulminari contingeret. Deinde misit rex ad Iulium, responsa concilij sui: petens ut vel paci acquiesceret, vel usquâ generale concilium indiceret, ad hanc materiam exactius pertractandam. Neutrum tamen admisit Iulius, Cæsari Iulio quàm Petro Apostolo similior: sed Ludovicum fulmine suo perculit, eiusq; regnū in praedam exposuit, & sequeti anno egregius tel-lator mortuus est.
units.tr: At that time there was at Pavia a jurist of great name, Philippus Decius, who published a writing and defended the cardinals' cause against the pontiff. From the twentieth book of the Chronicles of Massei: The king of the Franks, understanding that Pope Julius, in league with the Venetians, was plotting something against his men, who were stationed in garrisons, convened a council at Tours in the month of September, where these questions were put forward: Is it lawful for the pope to make war on any prince without cause? And may such a prince, in defending his own, attack the aggressor and withdraw from his obedience? The reply was: It is not lawful for the pontiff; but it is lawful for the prince to do what was asked. The Pragmatic Sanction was also to be observed throughout the kingdom of France. Nor should one care about unjust censures, should it happen that one was struck with thunderbolts. Then the king sent to Julius the answers of his council, asking that he either accept peace or summon a general council, to treat this matter more exactly. Julius, however, admitted neither, being more like Julius Caesar than the apostle Peter; but he struck Louis with his thunderbolt, exposed his kingdom to plunder, and in the following year died, an excellent layer of snares.

units.la: De quo sequens epigramma Conradus Grebelius fecit:
units.tr: Conrad Grebel wrote the following epigram about him:

units.la: Genua cui patrem, genitricem Græcia, partum Pontus & unda dedit: hic bonus esse potes? Fallaces Ligures, mendax est Græcia, Ponto Nulla fides. In te hæc singula Iule tenes.
units.tr: Genoa gave him a father, Greece a mother, the sea and the waves gave him birth: can you be good, you who are of this sort? The Ligurians are deceitful, Greece is a liar, there is no faith in the Pontus. You, Julius, hold all these qualities in yourself.

units.la: De hoc Iulio legitur in quodam Commētario magistrorum Parisiensium contra Lutheranos, quòd duobus nobilissimi generis adolescentibus, quos Anna Galliarum regina Roberto Nanetensi Cardinali informandos commiserat, & aliis multis, diabolica rabie (proh facinus) stuprum intulerit. Simile quiddam ab alio scriptore narratur, cui prædictus Grebelius hoc addidit distichon: Venit in Italiam, spectabilis indole rara, Germanus: rediit de puero mulier. Animus certè abhorreret, hæc sanctissimorum cœ-libum facta referre, nisi tam atrociter Dei filium in suis innocentissimis membris trucidarent.
units.tr: Of this Julius it is read in a certain commentary of the Paris masters against the Lutherans that he inflicted rape, by diabolical fury (what a deed!), on two adolescents of most noble family, whom Anne, queen of the French, had committed to Cardinal Robert of Nantes to be taught, and on many others. Something similar is related by another writer, to whom the aforesaid Grebel added this couplet: A German came into Italy, of remarkable and admired character; he returned from a boy into a woman. My mind would certainly shrink from recounting these deeds of the most holy celibates, unless they had so savagely slaughtered the Son of God in his most innocent members.

units.la: Georgius Lilius, in Anglorum regum chroni-co, gloriatur Henricum septimum hanc adorasse Babylonicam bestiam, ac monstrum Sodomiticum, his verbis: Anno, inquit, Domini 1504. rex oratores tres, ad præstandam Iulio Secundo pontifici Rom. de more obedientiam, Romam mittit. Nec eo quicquam celebrius, opinione sua, inuenire in Anglorum historiis poterat, quo illum illustraret annum. Sed ita adulari norunt papistæ, ipsissimis Antichri-stis ac diaboli vicarijs, ut patriam, imò veritatem atq; Christum ipsum pro ventre prodant. Longè aliter egisse Coletum, apud Erasmum in vita ip-sius legimus, qui in concione ad regè dicebat, quòd Angli Christum potius agnoscerent principem, quàm aut Iulios aut Alexandros. Sed in supputatione vehementer Lilius errat: dum pro 23 regni sui anno 19. assumit, O perfidissimi gancones,po-tius Gomorrhiones. Ex Volaterrano & Tempo-rum sasciculo: Prædistus Iulius, anno Domini 1504 matronam quandam Romanam, nomine Fran-cisciscam[?],canonizauit, ob id quod voluptatem inui-ti coitus, ardente supra vuluam lardo posito, re-primere solebat. Ex Leandro & Mantuano: Sub eodem Iulio noua haeresis orta est, super loco con-ceptionis Christi in virgine matre. Rtolemaeus[?] qui-dam Lucensis, Cisterciensis ordinis monachus, in quodam templo Mantuae praedicabat, Christum su-isse iuxta cor eiusdem virginis ex tribus guttulis sanguinis conceptum, & non in utero, ut alij, iuxta communem naturae ordinem, hunc statim in ignem coniiciendum esse iudicabant Hieronymus Fauen-tinus & alij Dominicani, haereticorum magistri. At Baptista Mantuanus mitius cum illo agendum fo-re decernebat, quum non ex malicia, sed praecipiti quadam ac licentiosa ignorantia, id protulerit. un-de idem Baptista libellum scripsit, de vero Christi conceptionis loco per scripturas: & inde extin-ctus est ille stultissimus error, ex hypocritico mo-nachorum ocio natus.
units.tr: George Lilly, in his chronicle of the kings of the English, boasts that Henry VII adored this Babylonian beast and Sodomitic monster, in these words: In the year, he says, of the Lord 1504, the king sends three ambassadors to Rome, to render the customary obedience to Julius II, the Roman pontiff. Nor, in his opinion, could he find anything more famous in the histories of the English by which to make that year illustrious. But the papists know how to flatter so, being the very Antichrists and vicars of the devil, that they betray their country, or rather truth itself and Christ himself, for the belly's sake. We read in Erasmus, in his life, that Colet acted quite differently, who in a sermon said to the king that the English should acknowledge Christ rather as prince than either Julius or Alexander. But in his reckoning Lilly errs greatly, while for the twenty-third year of his reign he takes the nineteenth, O most faithless catamites, rather Gomorrhites. From Volaterranus and the Fasciculus of Times: The aforesaid Julius, in the year of the Lord 1504, canonized a certain Roman matron, named Francisca, because she used to restrain sexual desire by the unwilling act of coition, with lard placed upon her womb while it burned. From Leandro and Mantuanus: Under the same Julius a new heresy arose concerning the place of Christ's conception in the Virgin Mother. A certain Ptolemy of Lucca, a Cistercian monk, was preaching in a church at Mantua that Christ had been conceived beside the heart of the same Virgin from three little drops of blood, and not in the womb, as others hold, according to the common order of nature. Hieronymus Faventinus and other Dominicans, masters of heretics, judged that he should at once be cast into the fire. But Baptista Mantuanus decided that he should be treated more gently, since he had put this forward not from malice, but from a certain hasty and licentious ignorance. Whence the same Baptista wrote a little book on the true place of Christ's conception from the Scriptures; and so that most foolish error, born of the hypocritical idleness of monks, was extinguished.

units.la: Iulius iste, bellator insignis, cum exercitu, ut dictum est, egrediens urbem, petri clauem in Tyberim proiecit, hisce verbis: Quia clauis S. petri non amplius valet, valeat gladius S. pauli. De quo Gilbertus Ducherius:
units.tr: This Julius, a notable warrior, going out of the city with his army as has been said, threw the keys of Peter into the Tiber with these words: Since the keys of St Peter no longer avail, let the sword of St Paul avail. Of him Gilbert Ducherius writes:

units.la: In Gallum, ut fama est, bellum gesturus acerbum, Armatam educit Iulius urbe manum:
units.tr: As report has it, about to wage a bitter war against the Gaul, Julius leads an armed band out of the city.

units.la: Accinctus gladio, claues in Tibridis amnem Proiicit, & sæuus talia uerba facit: Quum Petri nihil efficiant ad prælia claues, Auxilio Pauli forsitan ensis erit.
units.tr: Girded with a sword, he throws the keys into the river Tiber and, fierce, speaks such words: "Since Peter's keys achieve nothing in battle, perhaps the sword will be of help with Paul's aid."

units.la: Quo facto (inquit Bibliander) Iulius Papa Tiberino flamini resignauit omne ius, si quod habuerunt Papæ Romani à Petro, cui dixit Dominus: Et tibi dabo claues regni cœlorum. Etenim qui claues, symbolum potestatis, abiecit ac respuit, se & successores haereditate quocq; Petrina exuit ac spoliauit.
units.tr: By this act (says Bibliander), Pope Julius gave up to the Tiber god every right that the Roman popes had, if they had any, from Peter, to whom the Lord said: "And I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven." For he who cast away and rejected the keys, the symbol of power, stripped and despoiled himself and his successors also of the inheritance of Peter.
163. LEO the Tenth.

units.la: Leo decimus, patria Florentinus, ex clarissimo Mediceorum genere natus, & Ioannes Medices ante Papatum dictus, diaconus olim Cardinalis S. Mariæ in Dominica, à Cardinalibus præter omnem expectationem in demortui Iulij suffectus est locum. Bonis literis à prima iuuentute diligenter institutus, doctissimisq; præceptoribus usus, Angelo præsertim Politiano, uiro utriusq; linguæ Græcæ & Latinæ callentissimo: eruditos homines deinceps supra modum semper amauit. Decimoter-tio ætatis suæ anno, ab Innocentio octauo fiebat Cardinalis, & anno tricesimo octauo pontifex Romanus. Fuit hic Leo natura ipsa quietus ac mitis, sed ab inquietis & immitibus plerunq; gubernatus: tus: quorum arbitratu pleraq; insolenter passus est agi. Delicatulo corpori deditus ocio, carnem suam ad voluptatem nutriuit immanis mundi deside rijs, et amoenis ad libidinem iucunditatibus. Musicos ac uinas inter lautitias, ad animum in mensa exhilarandum, in summis deliciis habuit: sed Euan gelium regni Dei, ut alter Caiphas, implacabili odio in Luthero atq; aliis prosecutus est. Proponen-ti enim semel Cardinali Bembo quiddam ex laetoil lo Dei nuncio, dissolutè respondebat: Quantum nobis ac nostro coetui profuerit ea de Christo fabula, satis est seculis omnibus notum. Sceleratissimum nebulo propalàm expressit, se Antichristum illum esse, quem Paulus peccati hominem ac perditionis filium vocat. Largissimas indulgentias, et easdem eptissimas, pro nummis ad voluptatem haurien-dis, scortis alendis, spurijsq; ditandis, currentibus per regna Christiana sine numero fraterculis, spar-sit.
units.tr: Leo the Tenth, a Florentine by birth, born of the most illustrious family of the Medici, called John de' Medici before his papacy, once a deacon-cardinal of Santa Maria in Dominica, was raised by the cardinals to the vacant place of the dead Julius, contrary to all expectation. Diligently educated in good letters from his earliest youth, and taught by most learned tutors, above all Angelo Poliziano, a man very skilled in both Greek and Latin, he always afterwards loved learned men beyond measure. In the thirteenth year of his age he was made a cardinal by Innocent the Eighth, and in the thirty-eighth year of his life he became Roman pontiff. This Leo was by nature quiet and gentle, but he was for the most part governed by restless and harsh men, and at their direction he allowed many things to be done shamelessly. Given over to a pampered body and to idleness, he fed his flesh for pleasure with the desires of the vast world and with the agreeable delights of lust. He held in the highest favour musicians and wines among the luxuries, to cheer the spirit at table; but the gospel of the kingdom of God, like another Caiaphas, he pursued with implacable hatred, above all against Luther and others. For once, when Cardinal Bembo put forward something from the joyful messenger of God, he answered loosely: "How much that fable about Christ has profited us and our company is known well enough to all ages." He openly declared, most wickedly, that he was that Antichrist whom Paul calls the man of sin and the son of perdition. He scattered very lavish indulgences, and most easily obtained, to draw in money for pleasures, to feed prostitutes and to enrich bastards, while countless little friars ran through the Christian kingdoms.
Conrad Grebel against Cajetan.

units.la: Germanos, decimas tunc cum extorquere parabat, Qualem oratorem iussit adire Leo? Dimisit quendam, labor esset dicere qualem: Nimirum uerbo est dicere sat, Monachum. Tot aureorum nummorum millia, Samson Fr antifcanus[?] ille Mediolanensis, per eas in uarijs ter-ris collegit, ut mundus super eo prodigio valde ad miraretur. Supra 1200000 enim ducatorum summa erat, quos uno die pro Papatu emendo obtulit.
units.tr: When he was preparing to extort tithes from the Germans, whom did Leo order to approach as envoy? He sent a certain man, it would be hard to say what sort: a monk, to put it briefly. So many thousands of gold coins did that Samson Frantiscanus of Milan collect in various lands by these means, that the world was greatly amazed at that marvel. For the sum offered in a single day for buying the papacy was over 1,200,000 ducats.

units.la: Triginta & unum uno die Cardinales creauit Leo, ingenti corrasa pecunia, & uiis eo ipso die horribilibus portentis. Anno Domini 1521 quo Rhodum expugnabat Solymannus, in ipsis Christi natalibus, dum suum exiret conclaue, ad primam in aurora Missam celebrandam, subita post tergum eius, tectum quoddam marmoreum pulcherrime exstructum cecidit, ac multi ex eius satellitio inde perierunt. Hoc omine significauit Deus, Papatum ob atrocia & infanda in eo flagitia breui periturum.
units.tr: Leo created thirty-one cardinals in one day, having gathered a great sum of money, and on that very day there were dreadful portents. In the year of the Lord 1521, when Suleiman was storming Rhodes, on the very feast of Christ's nativity, as he was leaving his chamber to celebrate the first Mass at dawn, a marble roof, beautifully built, suddenly collapsed behind him, and many of his attendants perished there. By this omen God signified that the papacy, because of its atrocious and unspeakable crimes, would soon perish.

units.la: Spurios suos ille mirum in modum ditauit, atq; fi-mil ad utriusq; ordinis Principatus, aliorum iniu-ria, sublimauit. Iulianum nempe, quem dicunt ex sorore nepotem, Mutinensem ducem creauit: & Laurentianum[?], Vrbini ducem: adiunctis uxoribus, Cardi Sabaudi sorore uni, & Bononiae ducibus alteri. Nam ducem Vrbinatem ducatus possessione priuauerat, ut horum unum in eius substituerat locum. In ducem quoque Ferrariensem similia tentabat: sed frustra. Iulium uero nepotem, Cardinale constituit. Anno Domini 1521. & prima die Decembris, ut studiuerat Gallos à Cesarianus sua etiā opera Me diolani superatos, cæsos, captos & ab Italia pulsos, inter pocula supra modum lætus ac ridens, spiritum effluisse dicitur, cum nec cœlum nec infernum post hanc vitam esse crederet. De hoc Leone Actius Sannazarius sic scribit:
units.tr: He enriched his bastards in a wonderful manner, and raised them to the principalities of both orders, to the injury of others. Indeed he made Giuliano, whom they say was the nephew of his sister, duke of Modena; and Lorenzo, duke of Urbino, with wives added: one was given the sister of the Duke of Savoy, and the other became duke of Bologna. For he had stripped the Duke of Urbino of his duchy, so that he might put one of these in his place. He also tried similar things against the Duke of Ferrara, but in vain. Julius, his nephew, he made a cardinal. In the year of the Lord 1521, on the first day of December, as he had striven, with his efforts also, to have the Gauls, overcome, slain, captured and driven out of Italy by Caesar's Milan, he is said, beyond measure joyful and laughing among his cups, to have breathed out his spirit, since he believed that there was neither heaven nor hell after this life. Concerning this Leo, Actius Sannazarius writes thus:

units.la: Sacra sub extrema, si forte requiritis, hora / Cur Leo non poterat sumere? Vendiderat.
units.tr: In the last hour, if perchance you ask, why could Leo not take the sacred rites? He had sold them.
A Pasquil on Leo:

units.la: Pastor ut ambiguo Proteus dignoscitur ore, / Et dubius liquidis sæpe vagatur aquis:
units.tr: As the shepherd is known by his changeable face, like Proteus, and often wanders in uncertain waters,

units.la: Sic Leo nulla fides tibi, nec constantia rebus, / Factaq; promissa sunt odiosa tuis.
units.tr: so, Leo, there is no faith in you, nor constancy in your affairs, and the promises made are hateful to your people.

units.la: Nec bona, nec mala sunt dubio credenda Leoni, / Est etiam in verum ut vix adhibenda fides.
units.tr: Neither good nor bad things are to be trusted to the doubtful Leo; there is even scarcely any faith to be given to the truth.

units.la: Quum ventrem imprudens avido natura Leoni / Fecisset, rimas præbuit huic geminas.
units.tr: When nature, carelessly, had made the greedy Leo's belly, she gave it two cracks.

units.la: Non excrementis fuerat satis una: sed harum / Altera nunc clausa, nec minus illa vorat.
units.tr: One was not enough for the excrements; but now one of them is closed, and the other devours no less.

units.la: Gaude Roma, brevi hac solveris peste: fastidiet[?] / Alvum, tam magni ponderis impatiens.
units.tr: Rejoice, Rome: you will soon be released from this plague; the belly, impatient of so great a weight, will loathe it.

units.la: Differat à Decimo quàm Iulius ipse Leone, / Discere ab amborum nomine Roma potest.
units.tr: Rome can tell by the names of the two how far Julius himself differs from the tenth Leo.

units.la: Iulius est hominis, bruti Leo. Iulius egit, / Quæ suasit ratio: quod libet, iste facit.
units.tr: Julius is of man, Leo of beast. Julius did what reason advised; this one does whatever he pleases.

units.la: Nota hoc loco, quòd anno à Christi incarnatio-ne 261. quum Paulus Samosatenus in Ecclesia Christianorum prima, quæ erat Antiochiæ, episcopale accepisset cathedram, in Christum Dei filium blasphemias statim euomuit, negans eum verum atq; æternum esse Dei filium. Quæ hæresis omnium pestilentissima, per Arrium, Mahumetem, & Antichristum Papam, in hodiernum fere diem est adaucta. Monachi etiam, qui quasi eodem anno sub Eremita Paulo initium habuerunt, in variis vitæ generibus & doctrinis eandem hæresim, Satana iugerente, fouebant, Antichristo in Dei templo regnante, vel publico in Ecclesia docendi munere fungente, quadraginta duobus mensibus, Apoc. ii. vel diebus 1260. quod idem est. Qui dies, ut par est, pro annis accepti, addito priore numero 261 annorum, ad annum usq; à Christo nato 1521 peruenit. Mysterium intellige. In eo enim anno plene reuelatum est ille aduersarius Dei magnus, qui sese extollebat super omne quod dicitur Deus, aut colitur. 2. Thess. 2. In eo, inquam, error ille sub Antichristi tyrannide aduersus Dei filium tot mortibus munitus, labefactari incepit: manifestata veritate ac fidei iustitia per spiritum Christi, piorum aliquot doctorum fideli ministerio. Anno nempe prædicto, Domini sci licet 1521. quo & dictus Leo obiit, coram ipso Romano imperio Vuormatiæ congregato, Lutherus nocte omnium, veram de Christo doctrinam, quam præfati negabant hæretici, in spiritu fortitudinis Dei intrepidè confessus est. Et ex vera illa confes-sione, vera Christi ecclesia renouari denuò cœpit, & eius regnum subinde maiores accipere uires: Anti-christi uero statim confici, et ad interitum perduci.
units.tr: Note here that in the year 261 after the incarnation of Christ, when Paul of Samosata had received the episcopal chair in the first church of the Christians, which was at Antioch, he at once spewed out blasphemies against Christ, the Son of God, denying that he was the true and eternal Son of God. This heresy, the most pestilent of all, was increased through Arius, Mahomet and the Antichrist Pope, down to almost the present day. The monks too, who began about the same year under the hermit Paul, in their various kinds of life and doctrines cherished the same heresy, Satan urging them on, while Antichrist reigned in the temple of God or discharged the office of public teaching in the Church, for forty-two months, Rev. 11, or 1260 days, which is the same thing. These days, as is fitting, were taken for years, and with the earlier number of 261 years added, they reach the year 1521 after the birth of Christ. Understand the mystery. For in that year that great adversary of God, who exalted himself above everything that is called God or worshipped, was fully revealed, 2 Thess. 2. In that year, I say, that error, fortified by so many deaths under the tyranny of Antichrist against the Son of God, began to be shaken, the truth and the righteousness of faith being made manifest through the Spirit of Christ and the faithful ministry of several pious teachers. In the aforesaid year, namely 1521, in which the said Leo also died, Luther, before the Roman empire itself assembled at Worms, fearlessly confessed in the Spirit of God's strength the true doctrine about Christ, which the aforesaid heretics denied. And from that true confession the true Church of Christ began to be renewed again, and its kingdom gradually received greater strength, while Antichrist was at once being overthrown and brought to ruin.

units.la: Ex Christiano Massaeo: Anno Domini 1515 Frācifcus[?] Gallorum rex accepit à Leone Iubileum (venales indulgentias) diuulgandum per Gallias: qui & alia (Angliam in primis) Christiani orbis climata occupauit. Abyssus malorum. Nam sub umbra professionis in Turcas inæstimabiles thesauros collegerunt. Quorum conflatores & commissarij qui-dam, persuaserunt turbis, ut quicunque daret io solidos, liberaret animam pro qua daret, à poenis purgatorij. Nam pro regula certa tenebant, Dominum Deum facere quicquid ipsi uellent, secundum illud: Quicquid soluerit super terram, &c. Quod si uel iota minimum fuisset quàm io solidi, nihil prodesse concionati sunt. Displicebat hic quaestus sanctis Ecclesiæ filiis. Accepit quaestio ventilari de potestate vicarij: & unde hæc nouissima prælatis doctrina noua, quam prisci pontifices ignorassent? Erat tunc in Germania Martinus Luther, qui nimis acriter inuectus est in has indulgentias. Opposuit se illi Ioannes Eckius: uicissimq; bi[?] duo suggestum conscen-derunt, coram populo contentiosissimè disputan-tes. tes. Leo longo fulmine Martinum damnat hærese-os, & à cætu fidelium proiicit. Mox ille ad futurū concilium appellauit. tulit inde Leo libellos eius incendio tradi Romæ. Et ius pontificium, quas De cretales uocant, atq; decreta papalia, Vuittenbergæ Martinum combussit, dicens: Sicut fecerunt mihi, sic feci eis. Hæc Massæus. Residuum huius historiæ quære apud Sleidanum. Ad istum Leonem antea clamauerat Baptista Mantuanus, in quarto Fastorum libro, his uerbis:
units.tr: From Christian Massaeus: In the year of the Lord 1515 Francis, king of the Gauls, received from Leo a jubilee (indulgences for sale) to be published through France, which also occupied other regions of the Christian world, England above all. An abyss of evils. For under the cover of a profession against the Turks they gathered inestimable treasures. Some of their collectors and commissioners persuaded the crowds that whoever gave ten shillings would free from the punishments of purgatory the soul for which he gave it. For they held as a fixed rule that the Lord God does whatever they themselves wish, according to that saying: Whatever you loose upon earth, etc. And they preached that if it were even a tiny bit less than ten shillings, it would avail nothing. This gain displeased the holy sons of the Church. The question began to be debated concerning the power of the vicar: and whence was this newest doctrine, unknown to the early pontiffs, which the prelates taught? At that time in Germany there was Martin Luther, who attacked these indulgences too fiercely. John Eck opposed him, and the two mounted the platform, disputing most contentiously before the people. Leo condemned Martin of heresy with a long thunderbolt and cast him out of the assembly of the faithful. Soon afterwards he appealed to a future council. Leo then ordered his books to be handed over to the fire at Rome. And Martin burned at Wittenberg the pontifical law which they call the Decretals, and the papal decrees, saying: As they have done to me, so I have done to them. Thus Massaeus. Look for the rest of this history in Sleidan. Earlier, Baptista Mantuanus had cried out against this Leo in the fourth book of the Fasti, in these words:

units.la: Magna gerendarum superest tibi copia rerum, Sancte pater: rem magna animo complectere grandi. Sed tria præsertim restant cura atq; labore Digna tuo. Bellum est primum, quo sissa laborat Italia, & pleni humano iam sanguine campi. Est aliud, Romana graui maculata ueneno Curia, quæ spargit terras contagia in omnes. Postremum est oppressa fides, exposta rapinis Vndiq;, & in prædam populis proiecta cruentis. At te hæc subsidium magnis clamoribus erant. Sancte pater, succurre Leo, res publica Christi Labitur, ægrotatq; fides iam proxima morti.
units.tr: Great scope remains for you, holy father, to accomplish great deeds: embrace the matter with a great spirit. But three things especially remain, worthy of your care and labour. The first is war, by which Italy, cleft asunder, is in distress, and the fields are already full of human blood. The second is the Roman Curia, stained with grievous poison, which scatters contagion over all lands. The last is the faith, oppressed, exposed to plunder on every side, and thrown as prey to bloodthirsty peoples. To these things, with loud cries, you are our help. Holy father, Leo, hasten to our aid: the commonwealth of Christ is sliding, and the faith, sick, is near to death.

units.la: Ex diuersis Chronicis: Polonis anno Christi 1516.
units.tr: From various Chronicles: the Poles, in the year of Christ 1516.

units.la: Leo pontifex Iubilei gratiam uenalem dedit. Et sequendi anno, in uno die 31 Cardinales creauit.
units.tr: Pope Leo granted the grace of the Jubilee for sale. And in the following year, on a single day, he created 31 cardinals.

units.la: Quo die facta est Romæ tempestas ingens fulminis & tonitrui: quæ templum, in quo creati erant, percußit: atq; Iesum puerulum è gremio Deiparæ, & claues è manibus Petri excußit. Quod omè multi interpretabantur portendere ruinam sedis Ro-manæ, carminaq; acerba scripserunt in eadem. Ex hac Cardinalium creatione (inquit Valerius Anselmus) ac nummarijs indulgentijs, dispensationibus, priuilegijs, sacerdotijs et alijs, ingenti corraso nummo, agnatos numularios dotauit, atq; simul ad utriusq; ordinis principatus aliorum iniuria cuexit.
units.tr: On the day on which these were made, a huge storm of lightning and thunder arose at Rome, which struck the church in which they had been created, and shook from the arms of the Mother of God the little Jesus, and from the hands of Peter the keys. Many interpreted this as portending the ruin of the Roman see, and wrote bitter verses about it. From this creation of cardinals (says Valerius Anselmus), and from money-making indulgences, dispensations, privileges, priesthoods and other things, having heaped up enormous sums of money, he endowed his relatives the moneychangers, and at the same time raised them to the principality of each order, to the injury of others.

units.la: Eodem anno quo hæc sunt facta, Martinus Luthe-rus, theologus summus, ut prædictum est, veram fidem contra hypocrisim, docere incepit: Papatuq; deinceps paulatim corruere non desijt. Leo autem nono sui pontificatus anno, & prima die Decem-bris, cum ex nuncio accepisset in cœna, Gallos ab Italia pulsos, et inde inter pocula lætaretur, in hæc prorumpens verba: Tria beneficia contulit mihi Dominus: primum, quòd exul a patria, Florentiam cum gloria redij: secundum, quòd Apostolicus dici merui: tertium, quòd auxilio Gallos effugaui: læta febre correptus, obiter expirauit. Aliud Chroni-con habet, quòd attonito morbo subito corruerit. In cuius laudem poeta eius temporis hoc edidit.
units.tr: In the same year in which these things were done, Martin Luther, a most eminent theologian, as has been said, began to teach the true faith against hypocrisy; and from then on the papacy did not cease gradually to collapse. But Leo, in the ninth year of his pontificate, on the first day of December, having received news at dinner that the French had been driven out of Italy, and rejoicing over it among his cups, burst out in these words: "The Lord has bestowed three benefits upon me: first, that, an exile from my country, I returned to Florence in glory; second, that I have deserved to be called Apostolic; third, that with help I have put the French to flight." Seized by a joyful fever, he died shortly afterwards. Another Chronicle has it that he fell suddenly, struck by a stupor. In his praise a poet of that time published this:

units.la: Differat a decimo quàm Iulius ipse Leone,
units.tr: Let Rome decide how far Julius himself differs from the tenth Leo,

units.la: Discere ab amborum nomine Roma potest. [?]ulius est hominis, bruti Leo Iulius egit Quæ suasit ratio, quod libet, iste facit.
units.tr: she can learn from the names of the two. Julius was a man, Leo a brute. What reason urged, Julius did; whatever he pleases, this one does.

units.la: Sub hoc Leone, anno Domini 1516 obijt Bapti-sta Mantuanus, omnium qui unquam fuerunt fraterculorum doctissimus, anno ætatis suæ 72. Ille est (ut ad Burellum Bostius scribit) qui seculo O-ctauiano, tot uatibus superbo, obijt merito positus: & quo mille ab hinc annis, nemo aut pulchrius aut dulcius, poema scripsisse legatur. uitæ seueritate, morumq; sanctitate clarus, ac disciplinarum omnium scientissimus. Res diuinas, nullo inuitatus Me-cœnate, cecinit: ut etiam absentes consolaretur, di-uinus homo. Is multis in locis affirmat, non omnia sibi placere quæ Romana ecclesia, pro fide credendæ offert: licet ea aliquando & ipse scriptis co-probauerit. De quibus in lib. 12. Fastorum sic ait: Et licet his olim nugis iuuen liter aures Præbuerim: tamen ut melius cū tempore factum est Iudicium, lis hæc mihi perniciosa uideri Cœpit, & ex grauium cuneis abigenda uirorum.
units.tr: Under this Leo, in the year of the Lord 1516, died Baptista Mantuanus, the most learned of all the little friars who have ever existed, in the seventy-second year of his age. He is (as Bostius writes to Burellus) the one who, deservedly placed in the Augustan age, proud of so many poets, died; and, than whom in the thousand years since, no one has been read to have written a more beautiful or sweeter poem. Renowned for the severity of his life and the sanctity of his morals, and most skilled in all the disciplines, he sang of divine things, invited by no Maecenas, so that he might console even those who were absent; a divine man. In many places he affirms that not everything which the Roman church offers to be believed as faith pleases him, although at times he himself approved those things in his writings. Concerning these he says thus in book 12 of the Fasti: "And although I once lent my ears to these trifles in my youth, yet, as judgement has been better formed with time, this dispute began to seem pernicious to me, and to be driven out from the ranks of grave men."

units.la: Detestatur ille multas in papismo abusiones iniquas, ac peracriter insectatur: nec demum parcit eorum sacrosanctis sacrificijs & missis, sed dicit esse insipida sacra, altariaq; eorum passim for-dere. In Ecloga nona docet, omne ferarum genus habere romæ suas aras, & omnem uitiosorum hominum colluuie illic esse in honore ac precio. Multa taq; profert in aspernationem auaritiæ ac tyranni dis eiusdem Romæ curiæ, dicens inter alia:
units.tr: He detests the many unjust abuses in Papism and attacks them most bitterly; nor does he finally spare their most sacred sacrifices and masses, but says that their rites are insipid, and everywhere he undermines their altars. In the ninth Eclogue he teaches that every kind of wild beast has its altars at Rome, and that every sort of vicious men is held in honour and value there. He brings forward many things to the disparagement of the avarice and tyranny of the Roman Curia, saying among other things:

units.la: Mille lupi, totidem vulpes in vallibus ipsis Lustra tenet. Et quod dirum ac mirabile dictu est, Ipse homines (huius tanta est violentia cœli) Sæpe lupi effigiem moresq; assumere vidi, Inq; suum sevire gregem, multaq; madere Cæde sui pecoris. Factum vicinia ridet, Nec scelus exhorret, nec talibus obviat ausis.
units.tr: A thousand wolves and as many foxes hold their dens in the very valleys. And what is dreadful and wonderful to tell, I have often seen men themselves (so great is the violence of this sky) take on the likeness and manners of wolves, and rage against their own flock, and drench themselves with much slaughter of their own sheep. The neighbourhood laughs at the deed, nor does it shudder at the crime, nor does it oppose such daring.

units.la: Sæpe etiam miris apparent monstra figuris, Quæ tellus affecta malis influxibus edit. Sæpe canes tantam in rabiem vertuntur, ut ipsos Vincant cæde lupos: & qui tutela fuerunt, Hostiles ineunt animos, & ovilia mactant.
units.tr: Often too there appear monsters in wondrous shapes, which the earth, affected by harmful influences, brings forth. Often dogs are turned to such rage that they overcome the wolves themselves by slaughter; and those who were the guardians become hostile in spirit and butcher the sheepfolds.
Against Rome, from the fifth Eclogue.

units.la: Si quid Roma dabit, nugas dabit. Accipit aurū, Verba dat, heu Romæ nunc sola pecunia regnat. Exilium virtus patitur, &c.
units.tr: If Rome gives anything, it gives trifles. It takes gold, it gives words; alas, at Rome now money alone reigns. Virtue suffers exile, etc.

units.la: In Romam, ex primo libro Sylvarum.
units.tr: Against Rome, from the first book of the Silvae.

units.la: Roma quid insanis toties? quid sanguine gaudes? Quid geris imbelli spicula tanta manu? Quo vesana ruis? studioq; armaris inani, Iam senio lassas debilitante manus? Nec potes antiquos belli nescire tumultus,
units.tr: Rome, why do you rage so often? Why do you delight in blood? Why do you grasp such weapons with a hand unfit for war? Where do you rush in your frenzy, and arm yourself in vain, when your hands are already weary and weakened by old age? Nor can you forget the ancient uproars of war.

units.la: Nec solitam rabiem longa senecta domat. Si foris arma tacent, tu bella domestica tentas, Nec feritas requiem ferre superba potest. Tu similis colubro: quoties gravis ira venenum Suscitat, & mota lumina bile rubent. Sic furis, ut spumis ex ore cadentibus atrox Fulmineo quoties dente minatur aper. Sic fremis, ut frendens, cum ferrea vincula mandit Cerberus, & stygias murmure turbat aquas.
units.tr: Nor does long old age tame your customary fury. If foreign arms are silent, you attempt civil wars at home, nor can your proud savagery endure rest. You are like a serpent: whenever grievous anger stirs up its poison, and its eyes glow red with stirred-up bile. You rage like a wild boar whose foaming mouth drips, and who threatens with a lightning-fast tusk. You roar like Cerberus when he gnaws his iron chains and troubles the Stygian waters with his growling.

units.la: Tu fratres in bella vocas, in pignora patres, Et scelus omne audes, & pari omne nefas. Fas & iura negas, homines & numina fallis: Nec Iovis imperium, nec Phlegethonta times. Singula texentem conuicia, deseret aetas: Tantum ac tale tuae est improbitatis onus. Romanus pater est Mauors, lupa Martia nutrix; Haec hominum mores ingeniumq; docent. Viuere qui sancte cupitis, discedite: Roma Omnia cum liceant, non licet esse bonum.
units.tr: You call brothers to war, fathers against their children, and you dare every crime and every wickedness alike. You deny divine law and human right, and you deceive both men and gods. You fear neither Jove's power nor Phlegethon. Though an age were to pass while I recount each of your insults, such is the burden of your wickedness, so great and so grave. Mars is the father of the Romans, and the Martian she-wolf their nurse; these teach the manners and character of men. You who wish to live righteously, depart! Although everything is permitted at Rome, it is not permitted to be good.
From the second book of the Fasti.

units.la: I pudor in villas, si non patiuntur easdem Et villae uomicas: Vrbs est iam tota lupanar.
units.tr: O modesty, if they do not allow the same to the villages and the villages' vices, the city is now wholly a brothel.

units.la: Idem de Hieronymo, Roma fugiente, lib.9.
units.tr: The same, on Jerome, when Rome was fleeing, book 9.

units.la: Hanc Deus indignam voluit te incurrere fraudem, Vt mala corrupta fugeres consortia gentis, Et Et fieres uiuens cœli de ciuibus unus.
units.tr: God willed that you should fall into this unworthy deceit, so that you might flee the evil companionship of a corrupt nation, and become living, one of the citizens of heaven.

units.la: De Antichristo uel Papatu, ex 2 lib.
units.tr: On Antichrist or the Papacy, from the second book.
Fasti: (he perishes

units.la: Monstrum immane, potens hominum tot millia 4a[?] Absorbere gula, quot sanguinolenta uolebat Scuities[?].
